title: Medical Translation & Patient Rights in Türkiye: What You Are Entitled To
seoTitle: Medical Translation & Patient Rights in Türkiye (2026)
metaDescription: Know your patient rights in Türkiye: informed consent in your language, independent interpreters, SABİM 184 complaints, and KVKK privacy rules.
quickAnswer: International patients in Türkiye have the legal right to informed consent in a language they understand, transparent medical records, and strict health-data privacy under Law No. 6698 (KVKK). If a dispute arises, foreign patients can contact the Ministry of Health's SABİM 184 line or the 24/7 International Patient Assistance Unit at +90 850 288 38 38.
category: Medical Travel to Türkiye — Independent Advisory & Safety (The ITO Standard)

body.text: Are licensed hospitals required to provide informed consent in your language?

Yes. Under Turkish healthcare law and the [Regulation on International Health Tourism and Tourist Health](https://adiyamaneah.saglik.gov.tr/EN-419655/regulation-on-international-health-tourism-and-tourist-health.html), authorised facilities must inform international patients about procedures, risks, alternatives, and expected recovery in a language they understand before obtaining signed consent. Signing a Turkish-only form you cannot read does not constitute meaningful consent.

Türkiye's updated 2025 health tourism framework—published in the Official Gazette (No. 32882) and outlined in [ClinicProf's 2026 regulatory overview](https://clinicprof.com/turkey-health-tourism-regulation/)—requires separate Ministry of Health authorisation for facilities and USHAŞ authorisation for intermediary agencies. As noted in [Safemedigo's 2026 patient rights summary](https://www.safemedigo.com/en/blogs/international-patient-rights-turkey-consent-privacy-medical-records), even where electronic consent systems are used, you retain the right to read the full text in your language, ask questions, or decline treatment before surgery.
Why is an independent medical interpreter different from a clinic sales coordinator?

A clinic sales coordinator is employed or paid by the provider to convert enquiries into booked procedures, whereas an independent interpreter works solely to translate clinical facts accurately without commercial incentives. Confusing the two roles is one of the most common mistakes international patients make.

Where can international patients file an official complaint (SABİM 184 / Ministry of Health)?

International patients have direct access to Turkish Ministry of Health oversight channels if a clinic breaches standards, withholds records, or fails to deliver agreed care. You can reach the Ministry of Health Communication Centre (SABİM) by dialling 184 inside Türkiye, or call the 24/7 [International Patient Assistance Unit Call Center (+90 850 288 38 38)](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN%2C69450/0-850-288-38-38-international-patient-assistance-unit-interpreting-and-call-center-continues-service.html).

Operated in cooperation with USHAŞ, the [International Health Services Call Center](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-90754/international-health-services-call-center-commences-service.html) provides 24/7 interpreting in six languages—English, German, Arabic, Russian, Persian, and French—for calls to 112 emergency services and 184 SABİM. Keep these documents ready before filing a complaint:

items: Signed consent forms and quotes: Copies of every English consent form and written treatment plan.
Official itemized invoice: Your tax-registered e-Arşiv Fatura, explained in our [medical payment guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/paying-for-medical-treatment-turkey).
Full discharge file: Operative notes, prescriptions, and imaging, covered in our [aftercare abroad guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/medical-aftercare-abroad-turkey).
Provider authorisation details: The facility's exact legal name and Ministry of Health certificate number.

body.text: What privacy rules (KVKK) protect your medical records in Türkiye?

Medical records in Türkiye are classified as special-category (sensitive) personal data under Türkiye's [Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK)](https://www.kvkk.gov.tr/Icerik/6649/Personal-Data-Protection-Law), enforced by the independent [Personal Data Protection Authority](https://www.kvkk.gov.tr/Icerik/6586/Personal-Data-Protection-Authority) in Ankara. Hospitals and clinics must protect your records strictly and cannot publish your before-and-after photos or clinical details on social media without your explicit, separate written consent.

Under Article 11 of KVKK, you have the right to know how your health data is processed, request copies or corrections, ask who received your data, and object to unlawful sharing. Never sign a bundled admission form that combines surgical consent with marketing photo permissions—ask to strike out or decline media-release clauses separately.

faq.q: Can I refuse to sign a consent form that is only in Turkish?
faq.a: Yes. Do not sign any medical or financial form you cannot read. Ask for a translated copy in your language and a clear verbal explanation from your treating doctor before signing.

faq.q: Can I still cancel treatment after paying a deposit or signing consent?
faq.a: Under Turkish patient rights law, you have the right to withdraw consent and decline elective treatment at any point before the procedure begins. Financial refund terms depend on your written booking agreement.

Yes. Foreign patients calling SABİM 184 or the dedicated International Patient Assistance Unit at +90 850 288 38 38 can access 24/7 interpreting in English, German, Arabic, Russian, Persian, and French.

faq.q: Can a Turkish clinic post my before-and-after photos without permission?
faq.a: No. Under KVKK (Law No. 6698), health data and identifiable patient photos require your explicit, informed consent. Always check admission paperwork carefully and decline media-release clauses if you want privacy.

faq.q: How can I verify that a Turkish clinic is legally authorised to treat foreign patients?
faq.a: Ask for the clinic's Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorisation Certificate and check that the legal entity name matches the bank account and invoice before paying.
